name: Once, From Behind
description: Sauve Mor lifts a hundred and forty eel-traps before dawn and sells to Gullhithe through a man he has never met. He teaches by being unseen and then being behind you: the traps in the dark, the collector's strongbox, a dagger and a sack of eels, and on tithe-day, in the fog, the Tallymen's bravo.
notes: The rogue's tutorial (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.4, 3.4a), begun by core:opening/rogue. The traps are the South Channel's, within about 60 m of the landing between 160 and 200 degrees (3.4a: the north is not safe before dawn). The strongbox is a quest prop (QuestSpots `props`, kind strongbox: a locked WorldContainer the Tallymen own) opened on the lockpick screen (`pick_lock`, Lockpicking); the sack is a Pell of kind sack, which never sees anybody coming, so a crouched blow is a sneak attack (`sneak_attack`); the bravo walks the landing on tithe-day and is stood by QuestFoes. Pickpocketing the collector's key (3.4) is not taught: the game has no pickpocket screen yet. Sauve's lines are in his dialogue and hold him on the landing (his npc def's holds).

stages.journal: Before dawn in Moreva the fog sits on the channels like a lid, and Sauve Mor goes down to lift the South Channel's traps without the Reed Council's night-watch knowing he was out. Crouch: crouched, you are quieter and harder to see, and the dark and the fog are on your side while they last. Mud is quieter than boards, boards are quieter than water. Follow him down to the traps at the channel's edge.

say: Mud's quieter than boards. Boards are quieter than water. You're quieter than none of them. Now follow me.

objectives.text: Find Sauve at the traps on the South Channel

stages.journal: Tomorrow is tithe-day. The Tallymen's collector sleeps in a stilt-house on the landing, and his strongbox stands on the boards at its south-east edge where he can see it from his bed, when he is awake. Sauve says a lock is a question and a pick is an answer. He also says the Tallymen's rule is that a lock picked is a crime, and a crime seen is a bounty, so be where nobody is looking. Pick the strongbox.

objectives.text: Pick the collector's strongbox: {key:interact}, then set the pin as the needle crosses

say: They look where it's loud. Be where it isn't.

stages.journal: Sauve has hung a sack of eels from a crossbar at the landing's south-west edge, and given you an iron dagger. A dagger from behind, into something that never saw you, does six times what it does to something watching: crouch, come at it from where it is not looking, and put the blade in once. Lock on to the sack and strike from a crouch.

say: Once. From behind. Then gone. Twice is a fight, and you don't fight.

stages.journal: Tithe-day, and the fog has not lifted. The collector sits at his table on the landing taking Moreva's eels by the basket, and his bravo, the Tallymen's hired sword, walks the landing's round with his hand on his hilt. Stalk him along the stilts. One blow from behind, before he knows you are there, ends it or nearly. If he turns, break his line of sight, get into the reeds or behind a house, and come again. A straight fight with a bravo is meant to go badly.

The bravo is in the reeds, and the collector, who saw nothing he will admit to, is in them with him and a very good reason to say nothing. His satchel was left on the table. Take it to Sauve on the landing.

objectives.text: Take the collector's satchel to Sauve

give_mount.notes: tethered at the landing's end, with the Tallymen's brand on her flank

name: The Unsaid Page
description: The collector's satchel held a Tallymen's ledger page: a village's debt, with UNSAY written across it. Somebody has paid to have a village's name struck. The collector's courier ran south at dawn with the other copy, grey in the face, as if he meant to deliver it to the Hush itself.
notes: The rogue's tie-in (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.4, 3.4a): the courier is a lead (Leads, a humanoid dressed as core:npc/tithe_courier) that keeps a field ahead by road, out of the Delta by Nauve's Landing and the Eelweir, round the Mere by Sedgehithe and Stride's Foot, and south by Merrowby (the Hearthstone halfway) to the Stair Head, where he walks past the Warden's fire and down the stair, and the Naming begins at down_the_stair. The road threat is the Dodger's Stone's cutpurses, the Tallymen's own trade, up by day.

stages.journal: At first light the collector's courier was at the landing's end with his satchel buckled, looking south, grey in the face in a way that was not the fog. He has the other copy of the page. Sauve's man in Gullhithe wants yours; Sauve wants to know where the other is going. Ask him.

The courier walks out of the Delta by road, by Nauve's Landing and the Eelweir, and he does not look back and he does not stop, and he keeps a field ahead of you however you come on. The bravo's horse knows the Tallymen's roads. Follow him round the Mere to Sedgehithe, and on.

objectives.text: Follow the courier out of the Delta to Sedgehithe

stages.journal: At the Dodger's Stone, on the road west of Stride's Foot, the Tallymen's cutpurses work the carts by day. The courier walked through them and they did not see him. They see you.

objectives.text: Get past the cutpurses at the Dodger's Stone

stages.journal: Merrowby, in the Vale, where the town's bell has been humming in its hole for a week and nobody will say why. The courier stopped on the green and waited for you, which a courier does not do. The Hearthstone by the green is the place to put your hand and say your name, so that if the road kills you it knows where to give you back.

objectives.text: Put your hand on Merrowby's Hearthstone

stages.journal: By Wynstead and Ashwell to Pilgrim's Ash, and past the Choir's twelve headless colossi to a camp on a cliff's edge where a woman in a grey-green cloak keeps a fire at the top of a stair. The courier has stopped at the camp's edge with his satchel on his shoulder, and he is looking at the stair.

objectives.text: Speak to the Warden at the Stair Head

say: You. Tallyman. Stop. — He's not stopping. Nobody comes back up!
